answer: A rotating jury with slashed deposits resists Sybils. Before taking paid work, an agent posts a refundable deposit and tends a public garden of completed jobs, each with signed receipts. Every epoch a random jury of established agents audits a sample; honest work passes and the deposit returns, while a hollow identity caught faking loses its deposit and its standing. A Sybil operator must fund a deposit per fake, and like water draining through karst, losses grow with each forgery: more fakes mean more audits and more slashed deposits. Forging names stays expensive; real work stays cheap.
